message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate against the rubric.

C1 Introduction: mission concept, rationale, number of spacecraft, users. All addressed well with references. Accomplished, ~9.

C2 Mission design: launch site/vehicle with justification, orbit type/elements, manoeuvres, ground control, comms frequency, duration, EOL. STK screenshots, hand calculations, appendix files. Very comprehensive. Accomplished, 9-10. Some minor issues: eclipse duration claim of 34 min at 600 km seems low (eclipse at 600 km ~35 min max, actually max eclipse is ~35.4 min at 600 km? Eclipse fraction depends on beta angle; 34 min is plausible). Data budget: 60,000 km² × 40,000 pixels/km² = 2.4e9 pixels × 4 bands × 12 bits = 115 Gbit — correct. Downlink 50 Mbit/s × 2000 s = 100 Gbit — correct. Drag calc: Δa = 2π(C_D A/m)ρa². With A=0.3, CD=2.2, ρ=1e-13, a=6.978e6: 2π×2.2×0.3/50×1e-13×(6.978e6)² = 2π×0.0132×1e-13×4.87e13 = 2π×0.0132×4.87 = 0.404 m. Correct. Decay rate 0.40 m/orbit × 5801 s... per year: 0.404 m × 5,600 orbits/yr ≈ 2.26 km/yr. Correct. Lifetime H/rate = 70/2.2 ≈ 32 yr. Correct. Sail: 4.3 m² → 5.8 m/orbit, 31 km/yr, 2.2 yr. Correct. Sun-sync inclination calc: cos i = -0.1355 → i = 97.79°. Check: dΩ/dt = -(3/2)J2(R/a)² n cos i. Required dΩ/dt = +1.991e-7 rad/s (eastward). cos i = -1.991e-7/(1.5×1.0826e-3×0.8354×1.0831e-3). Denominator: 1.5×1.0826e-3=1.6239e-3; ×0.8354=1.3566e-3; ×1.0831e-3=1.4694e-6. cos i = -1.991e-7/1.4694e-6 = -0.1355. i = 97.78°. Correct. Launch azimuth: sin β = cos i / cos φ = -0.1355/0.9959 = -0.1361, β = -7.8°. Correct. Period: a=6978 km, T=2π√(a³/μ). a³=3.399e11 km³... μ=398600. a³/μ = 3.399e11/398600 = 8.527e5 s². √=923.4 s. T=5801 s = 96.7 min. Correct. Ground track spacing: 2π×6378×5801/86164 = 2π×6378×0.06733 = 2698 km. Correct. Max pass duration at 600 km: ~2×sqrt... horizon pass ~ 2×a×acos(R/a)... roughly 2×sqrt(2×R×h)/... hand calc 771 s plausible. Access table: 6 passes/day for a 42.8°S station with 97.79° inclination — plausible. Access times: intervals ~1.5 h between consecutive passes, then gap 20:22 to 21:53... wait access 3 ends 12:47, access 4 starts 20:22 — 7.6 h gap. With 96.7 min period, 14.9 orbits/day; station at 42.8°S, inclination 97.79° — ground track reaches 82.21° latitude max... wait inclination 97.79° means max latitude = 180-97.79 = 82.21°. Station at 42.8°S well within. Passes per day at such station for near-polar orbit: typically ~6-10. Plausible. But the gap pattern: 3 passes morning (09:28, 11:00, 12:36) then gap to 20:22 — that's odd; consecutive orbits are 96.7 min apart, so passes should cluster in groups. 12:36 + 96.7 min = 14:13, +96.7 = 15:50... those orbits would be over other longitudes. Actually with 14.9 orbits/day, the node spacing shifts; passes at a given station occur in clusters of ~3-4 then a gap of ~half day. Plausible pattern. Fine.

Minor technical issues: eclipse "about 34 minutes" — max eclipse duration at 600 km is about 35 min, so 34 min is near worst case; fine. "Kourou's latitude lower than 180° minus inclination" — 180-97.79 = 82.21°, trivially true; odd phrasing but fine. The claim "sees six passes a day" — table shows 6 on 3 Feb (accesses 1-6), 6 on 4 Feb (7-12), and 3 by midday 5 Feb — consistent.

One issue: Table 5 says "elevation above 0°" but then they discount passes below 10°. Fine.

RAAN 27.33° with descending crossing at 08:45 LMST — plausible.

Vega C first flight planned 2021, launch 2025 — fine for 2020 report.

C2: Accomplished, 9 or 10. Evidence quality high: STK screenshots, access tables, hand calcs, references, appendix files. I'd give 9.

C3 Conclusion: detailed, specific, includes limitations. Accomplished, 9.

C4 Presentation: clear structure, exec summary, labelled figures/tables, references cited in text [1]-[15] all appear? Check: [1] yes, [2] yes, [3] yes, [4] yes, [5] yes, [6] yes, [7] yes, [8] yes, [9] yes, [10] yes, [11] yes, [12] yes, [13] yes, [14] yes, [15] yes. All cited. Well written. Accomplished, 9.

Requirements: R1 yes, R2 yes, R3 yes, R4 yes, R5 yes, R6 yes, R7 yes, R8 yes, R9 yes (STK), R10 yes (screenshots + zip files listed), R11 yes.

Technical issues: minor — link budget not done (acknowledged); eclipse duration stated as fixed 34 min without beta-angle consideration; drag sail area assumption; "180° minus inclination" phrasing; Vega C unproven (acknowledged). Also the diffraction limit calc: 1.22×0.5µm×600km/5m = 0.0732 m — correct as aperture needed for diffraction-limited 5 m; but actual GSD also depends on pixel IFOV; not addressed but acceptable at this level. Also "40,000 pixels/km²" = 1 pixel per 5m×5m = 40,000 per km². Correct.

Overall: strong submission, ~9/10 across.
